requirement: Expose Python functions as MCP tools with a FastMCP-like @mcp.tool() decorator that validates call arguments and reports tool failures as ToolError.
skeleton: A ToolError, a frozen Tool dataclass, and a FastMCP class with a registering tool decorator, sorted list_tools, and call_tool that validates arguments and chains failures.
caption: A FastMCP-style tool server written in the standard library with inspect, dataclasses, collections.abc and typing and no third-party imports. ToolError covers registration and call failures. Tool is a frozen dataclass with name, description, fn, params and required. FastMCP.tool returns a decorator that uses the function name unless a name is given, raises ToolError for a duplicate, reads parameters and the docstring with inspect, and returns the function unchanged. list_tools sorts by name. call_tool raises ToolError for an unknown tool, unexpected arguments or missing required ones, and wraps arithmetic, lookup, type and value errors in ToolError chained from the cause. The fixture asserts listing, the returned function, defaults and custom names, duplicates, malformed calls and wrapped failures.

plan.intent: Register MCP tools with a decorator
constraints: Registering a duplicate tool name raises ToolError
Parameters with defaults are optional; the rest are required
Unknown tools, unexpected arguments and missing arguments raise ToolError
Tool failures raise ToolError chained from the original exception

rationale.teaches: Derive the tool contract from the signature once at registration and validate every call against it before invoking the function.
rationale.why: An MCP client sends arbitrary JSON arguments, so silent overwrites, unchecked arguments and lost causes turn into confusing model-facing errors.

ops.docstring: A FastMCP-style server whose tools register through a decorator.

ops.source:
class ToolError(Exception):
    """Raised for registration conflicts and failed or malformed tool calls."""

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Tool:
    """A registered tool with its parameter names and required subset."""

    name: str
    description: str
    fn: ToolFn
    params: tuple[str, ...]
    required: tuple[str, ...]

candidates.why_wrong: Registering a second tool with the same name silently replaces the first.
Unexpected arguments reach the function and surface as a generic failure.
Parameters with defaults are marked required while mandatory ones are optional.
The wrapped ToolError hides the original exception instead of chaining it.
Tools are listed in registration order instead of sorted by name.
